info.name: WinX88 — NexusGGR
info.description:
# WinX88 ↔ NexusGGR

Every request carries at least one **saved example**. Examples marked
`(captured)` are real responses recorded against the dev database and the
live provider on 2026-10-17 — not hand-written.

## Setup
Set `baseUrl`, `adminToken`, `playerToken` in **Variables**.
The upstream folder additionally needs `agentCode` / `agentToken`.

## The parts
- **Catalog** — pull providers and games into `casino_games`.
- **Curation** — rules + per-game overrides deciding which tab a game lands in.
- **Home categories** — the chips on the player home.
- **Player** — launch URLs.
- **Seamless callback** — what Nexus POSTs to *us* at `/gold_api`.
- **Upstream** — calling `api.nexusggr.com` directly, for debugging.

## Two things that will bite you
1. **IP allowlist.** Nexus authorises by IP and rejects IPv6 even when the
   IPv4 address is whitelisted. `INVALID_IP` names the address it saw —
   read it, it is usually a different address than you expect.
2. **Deduplicate on `txn_id_v2`.** One bet can pay out over several
   transactions sharing one `round_id`. `txn_id` carries the round id until
   2026-10-15, the per-transaction value after, and `txn_id_v2` is removed
   on 2026-10-31.

request.description:
Calls Nexus live, so it doubles as the connectivity check. `INVALID_IP` here means this **server's** address is not on the Nexus allowlist.

**Auth:** admin

response.name: 200 INVALID_IP (captured)

request.description:
Upserts, so it is safe to re-run. Omit `providerCode` to sync everything.

**Paced at ~1.1s per provider** — Nexus allows one `game_list` per second — so a full sync is ~32s and may outlive a proxy timeout while still finishing server-side. A provider that fails lands in `skipped` rather than aborting the run, so always read that array.

**Auth:** admin

What is already in `casino_games`, grouped by provider and catalog type.

**Auth:** admin

response.name: 200 OK (captured)

request.description:
Catalog rows with their curation state. `derived_type` is what the sync worked out; `type` is what players see; `override_type` is non-null only when a human pinned it.

**Auth:** admin

response.name: 200 OK (captured)

request.description:
Ordered by priority then id. **First match wins.**

**Auth:** admin

What the rule **would** re-file, without doing it. Always preview: a loose pattern can move hundreds of games.

**Auth:** admin

Creates without `id`, updates with it. `pattern` is a case-insensitive substring unless `is_regex`. An invalid regex is rejected here rather than silently matching nothing later.

**Auth:** admin

response.name: 400 invalid regex (captured)

request.description:
Games the rule had re-filed revert on the next re-apply, because `derived_type` still holds what the sync originally worked out.

**Auth:** admin

Beats every rule. **Sending neither `type` nor `displayName` clears the override**, and the game falls back to the first matching rule, then to `derived_type`.

**Auth:** admin

Re-runs rules and overrides over the catalog with **no provider calls** — the cheap way to apply a rule change to games already imported. Always recomputes from `derived_type`, so deleting a rule genuinely reverts.

**Auth:** admin

What the player panel renders. `source` decides where the chip gets its games: `ALL`, `SLOT_PROVIDER`, `OROPLAY_GROUP`, `CATALOG` (a `casino_games.type` — how Nexus games surface) or `LINK`.

**Auth:** public

request.description:
Prefer hiding.

**Auth:** admin

`rtp` is optional (0–999, clamped) and is **dropped for live and sportsbook**, which ignore it. Omit it and the player's configured RTP in the Nexus panel applies.

`user_code` sent upstream is the player's **username** — the identity every `/gold_api` callback echoes back.

**Auth:** player

response.name: 400 provider rejected (captured)

request.description:
Sportsbook has **no game list** — `game_list` returns 0 games for it — so it launches through this route rather than from the catalog.

**Auth:** player

item.name: 05 · Seamless callback (Nexus → us)
item.description: What NexusGGR POSTs to **our** server. Always answer HTTP 200 with the outcome in the body: a 4xx/5xx makes Nexus retry after we already moved the money. We get **5 seconds**; a timeout, network error or non-2xx leaves the result unknown and the transaction may be re-sent with the same `txn_id_v2`.

request.description:
Return the balance even when it is `0`.

**Auth:** public

The detail object key **must match** `game_type`.

**Auth:** public

item.name: POST transaction — slot tumbling win (2nd credit)

request.description:
**The case that breaks naive dedup.** Same `round_id` and `txn_id` as the bet above, new `txn_id_v2`. Keying on the round id classes this as a replay and the player never gets the rest of their win.

**Auth:** public

A retry must return the **original balance with `status: 1`**, not an error — otherwise their ledger and ours diverge.

**Auth:** public

`info` is **stringified** JSON, not an object.

**Auth:** public

The only product live on this integration before the catalog sync.

**Auth:** public

Aviator and the other eight Spribe games.

**Auth:** public

`FH` is absent from the published docs but real on this account — omitting it rejects every fish bet.

**Auth:** public

item.name: 06 · Upstream NexusGGR (direct)
item.description: Calling `api.nexusggr.com` yourself, for debugging. One endpoint, one POST, `method` selects the operation. **Force IPv4** — Nexus rejects an IPv6 egress even when your IPv4 address is whitelisted.

request.description: Rate limited to **1 per second**.

response.name: 200 INVALID_IP (captured)

request.description: Rate limited to **1 per second** — this is what makes a full sync take ~32s. `game_list_v2` returns multilingual names for PRAGMATIC, PGSOFT, REELKINGDOM, FATPANDA, HABANERO and CQ9 (no Bengali).
`game_code` is optional for live providers (returns a lobby). An **empty** `lobby_url` is rejected — omit it instead.
